correctness.rationale: Bavula's automorphism decomposition applies over odd finite fields and gives the tangent-identity kernel U as the product with unique factors of the odd inner parameters modulo the odd center and the degree≥3 odd generator substitutions. The respective dimensions of their coordinate sets are h−1_{n odd} and n(h−n), giving the claimed u_n. For a diagonal tangent involution, eigenvalues on odd basis monomials are the signs (−1)^(number of negative generators in the monomial). For mixed signs, toggling membership of one positive and one negative generator is a parity-preserving sign-reversing bijection; this proves O_+=O_− as integer dimensions without inferring integer multiplicities from a trace modulo the characteristic. The top central odd monomial removed when n is odd has sign (−1)^b. The substitution coordinate space Hom(V,W) is acted on by conjugation via the linear representative and its fixed maps preserve sign spaces, giving a(O_+−a)+b(O_−−b). Uniqueness of the two factors gives |C_U(L)|=q^f. For L≠I, an involutive lift generates a complement to the odd-order U in U⋊<L>, so all lifts are U-conjugate and the number of lifts is |U|/|C_U(L)|. For L=I the only square-one element of U is the identity. Choosing the negative subspace and then its complement gives the Gaussian factor times q^(ab). Sign eigenspaces give the grading and recover the involution uniquely in odd characteristic, while conjugacy of tangent involutions at fixed b and of their lifts gives n+1 graded-isomorphism types. Independently at n=2, write a substitution as a linear part A and a column z of top-degree coefficients; the square condition is A²=I and (A+det(A)I)z=0. It gives 1, q²(q+1), q² for the three types, agreeing with the formula. In the mixed cases the leading total exponent is (n+1)2^(n−2)+1_{n odd,b even}−1_{n odd} with unit leading coefficient; b=n has exponent h−1_{n odd} and b=0 exponent zero, both strictly smaller than the maximum. This proves the stated limiting uniform laws.
residual_risks: The finite square tests are corroboration only. The verifier uses int.bit_count(), so a replay should use Python 3.10 or newer rather than relying on the verification note's Python 3.9 claim.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported claim is the census of actual finite-field square-one maps by tangent negative rank and the fixed-n parity selection as q grows. The automorphism-group decomposition, coprime conjugacy argument, and grading/involution correspondence are prior ingredients. The strongest inspected finite exterior-algebra record gives an unstratified-by-order fixed-space spectrum for n=2, not this census, and the close parity analogues concern commutative truncated polynomial algebras, not exterior algebras.
residual_risks: The finite-field graded-identity lead in the survey bibliography was not verified in full text and unindexed finite grading work may contain closer coverage. This is a bounded originality judgment, not a historical-priority certification.

value.rationale: The population of each grading symmetry type is a natural invariant not captured by knowing the number of conjugacy classes. It distinguishes the sizes of equally valid linearized grading types, and the limiting uniform law on only certain ranks comes from a single central odd monomial that is invisible to a crude order estimate. The exact all-rank counts and this parity-sensitive consequence go beyond a small-instance inventory.
residual_risks: The population law applies at fixed n as odd field order grows, not to characteristic two, infinite generator rank, or equivalence by graded polynomial identities.
